Dragonflies can catch up to 95% of the prey they hunt, making them some of the insect world’s top mosquito bouncers. An adult can eat 30 to 100 mosquitoes a day, which explains the nickname “mosquito hawks.”

The pest control starts underwater: dragonfly nymphs hunt mosquito larvae and pupae, sometimes eating over 100 larvae daily. Once airborne, adults use sharp eyesight, speed, and impressive mid-air manoeuvres to grab mosquitoes and other insects.

By cruising around ponds, lakes, and marshes, dragonflies also help keep flies, gnats, and midges in check, while supporting balance in their habitats.

🚀 Want to Become a Generative AI Engineer in 2026? Here’s Your Learning Roadmap.

GenAI is evolving fast. You don’t need 50 courses or every framework. Master these 10 skills in sequence. 👇

1️⃣ Transformers & LLM Fundamentals
Learn transformer architecture, self-attention, Q/K/V, multi-head attention, masking, tokenization, context windows, positional encoding, and how LLMs generate responses.
📚 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZhAz268Hdpw&t=784s

2️⃣ Embeddings & Vector Databases
Understand embeddings, semantic similarity, cosine similarity, nearest-neighbor search, vector indexing, and databases such as FAISS, Chroma, and Pinecone.
📚 Algorithms: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lvH_zPj2o04&t=156s
📚 Embeddings: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JsGwjwnl4hY
📚 Implementation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5kCE0l11ZHk

3️⃣ Prompt Engineering & Structured Outputs
Learn zero-shot and few-shot prompting, system prompts, context engineering, JSON outputs, prompt optimization, tool calling, and validation.

4️⃣ Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
Master document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, semantic and hybrid retrieval, metadata filtering, reranking, grounded responses, citations, and evaluation.
📚 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4Ax77tnW0e8
📚 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X0btK9X0Xnk

5️⃣ LangChain
Connect models with data, tools, and application logic using integrations, prompt templates, retrievers, structured outputs, RAG pipelines, and workflows.
📚 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pSVk-5WemQ0&list=PLKnIA16_RmvaTbihpo4MtzVm4XOQa0ER0

6️⃣ LangGraph & Agentic AI
Build stateful workflows using nodes, edges, state management, conditional routing, memory, human approval, tool execution, error recovery, and multi-agent orchestration.
📚 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yC36gN-rqjo&list=PLKnIA16_RmvYsvB8qkUQuJmJNuiCUJFPL

7️⃣ Cloud AI & Production Deployment
Explore Microsoft Foundry, Amazon Bedrock, model hosting, inference APIs, enterprise RAG, agent deployment, observability, monitoring, scaling, cost optimization, and access control.
📚 Krish Naik: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZP_U8eKBy2g
📚 Azure: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gKLEsHv8X6I&list=PLKN5-zCKJG7w-3gXIVptJV7sSi7fbQoBE
📚 AWS: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cTBGIKAckKE&t=880s

8️⃣ Evaluation, Security & Guardrails
Learn RAGAS, LLM-as-a-Judge, faithfulness, answer relevance, hallucination detection, prompt injection, data leakage, PII protection, testing, and regression evaluation.
📚 RAGAS: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J3M95E0LQl8
📚 Judge: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3FcYdRQPMCo
📚 Evaluations: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6W92_t9FveA&list=PLEneLIDJFpcA
📚 Injection: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DANRXYsT4Bs
📚 Guardrails: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7V1w5gnZ-kw

9️⃣ Model Context Protocol (MCP)
Understand Host, Client, Server architecture; tools, resources, prompts; transports; authentication; authorization; secure tool execution; and business-system integration.
📚 Anthropic: https://anthropic-partners.skilljar.com/introduction-to-model-context-protocol
📚 Gate Smashers: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GxHOSWxp7c0
📚 Chai aur Code: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dZyQNy3-HjU
📚 Krish Naik: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-UQ6OZywZ2I

🔟 Build Real-World GenAI Projects
Start with:
🛠 Post Generator: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qZ_J-Xg0QM4&list=PLeo1K3hjS3uvLuF4Tq1i1KqNM2QvIyzFK

Anthropic starts trading on the Nasdaq. And this is one of the most important events in the AI market in years.

The company priced its shares at $83, putting its valuation at around $1.5 trillion. The IPO raised more than $81 billion, making it the largest in history. Another $26 billion was invested separately by Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom, TSMC, and other companies across the same AI ecosystem.

And the timing of this listing couldn't have been better.

The day before yesterday, Nvidia once again posted insane numbers. Quarterly revenue came in at $115.8 billion, twice as much as a year ago. Data centers alone accounted for $107.6 billion. In other words, money is still pouring into AI infrastructure at an enormous scale.

But Anthropic reveals the other side of this story. The company is growing rapidly, but at the same time, it has already taken on nearly $900 billion in future commitments for computing capacity. Essentially, Nvidia and other companies are generating hundreds of billions in revenue today because Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and others keep building more data centers and buying more computing power.

And this creates a rather interesting dynamic. Nvidia sells infrastructure to Anthropic. Anthropic spends enormous amounts of money on it. And now Nvidia is also helping finance Anthropic so it can keep growing and buying even more infrastructure.

This doesn't mean demand is artificial. Anthropic's revenue is growing at an incredible pace, and demand for AI is very real. But today, for the first time, the market gets a chance to publicly value one of the biggest buyers of all this infrastructure.

That's why I wouldn't focus only on the price at which ANT opens trading today.

If Anthropic surges after its listing, the market will get yet another confirmation that investors are still willing to fund AI at practically any price.

But if one of the most anticipated IPOs of the decade starts to struggle, the questions will quickly spread to the entire supply chain. Because Nvidia's seemingly endless revenue growth is only possible as long as someone is willing to keep paying for the construction of all this infrastructure.

Today, we'll finally see how much the public market is willing to pay for it.
